description: Test your knowledge of how LLMs process text as tokens, what token IDs are, and common tokenization myths.

questions.question: What does an LLM actually receive when you type a sentence?
options: The raw English words directly
An array of token IDs (numbers)
A JSON object with grammar rules
questions.explanation: LLMs don't understand English words. Your text is broken into tokens by a tokenizer, each token gets a numeric ID, and that array of numbers is what the model processes.

questions.question: Is one word always equal to one token?
options: Yes, always — one word = one token
No — a word can split into multiple subword tokens
Only for English words, not for other languages
questions.explanation: 'Awesome' might become 'awe' + 'some' (2 tokens). 'Untrustable' might become 'un' + 'trust' + 'able' (3 tokens). It depends on the tokenizer's vocabulary, not grammar.

questions.question: What is Byte Pair Encoding (BPE)?
options: A way to encrypt LLM responses
A tokenization method that merges common character pairs into reusable tokens
A compression algorithm for images
questions.explanation: BPE starts from byte-level units and merges frequently occurring pairs into tokens. Common pieces like 'un', 'trust', 'able' become reusable across many words. OpenAI uses BPE tokenizers.

questions.question: Do token IDs carry semantic meaning?
options: Yes — similar meanings have similar token ID numbers
No — token IDs are just lookup numbers with no inherent meaning
Only for English tokens, not for code or emojis
questions.explanation: Token IDs are arbitrary numbers mapped through a vocabulary. ID 8123 for 'Dog' and 8521 for 'Grapes' aren't related numerically. Meaning comes from embeddings, not token IDs.

questions.question: Why does the same sentence in Hinglish often cost more tokens than in English?
options: Hinglish is banned by LLM providers
Hinglish text often tokenizes into more pieces — English is more token-efficient
Hinglish prompts are automatically charged double
questions.explanation: English is more efficiently represented in most tokenizers. The same meaning in Hinglish or Hindi may require more tokens, which means higher API cost and faster context window fill-up.

questions.question: What is a context window in an LLM?
options: The browser window where you chat with AI
The maximum amount of tokenized text the model can process at once
The time limit before your chat session expires
questions.explanation: Context window = short-term working memory. It includes system instructions, your messages, uploaded documents, and tool outputs — all counted in tokens. Exceeding it causes truncation or errors.

questions.question: Which of these is a common tokenization misconception?
options: Different models use different tokenizers
One visible emoji is always exactly one token
Tokens directly affect API cost
questions.explanation: Emojis can be multiple tokens. Other myths: one word = one token, token IDs represent meaning, larger context = perfect memory, more tokens = better results. Always verify with a tokenizer playground.
